tools.description: List editor window IDs, titles, buffer IDs, geometry, active window and side panels.
tools.name: list_windows

tools.description: Read up to 131072 selected characters and cursor offsets in an editor window; truncated reports a larger selection. coordinateSpace distinguishes source from rendered-markdown offsets; a pending Markdown view refuses the read. Defaults to the active window.

tools.name: debug_status

tools.description: Set automatic source following (initially true), or reveal source/stack/scopes/output from the shared session. Omitted follow is unchanged; false keeps asynchronous stops in the background. Any view requires the current generation; source/stack/scopes also require a stopped target. follow=true resumes future automatic following; use view=source to reveal now. Presentation does not resume, relaunch or advance generation.
tools.name: debug_present

tools.description: Launch the configured THC target, or a general DAP adapter JSON configuration. Fails if a session is already active.
tools.name: debug_launch

tools.description: Attach to a loopback DAP adapter (127.0.0.1:4711 by default).
tools.name: debug_attach

tools.description: Continue, step, pause or disconnect the current debug generation. Accepted does not mean the next stop has occurred; inspect status afterwards.
tools.name: debug_control

tools.description: Run bounded goal-directed inspection and stepping with the selected System One supplier. Start requires an exact paused generation and a goal. Pause/stop revoke assistance and request a pause if running; reveal shows its evidence without stepping. Manual debugger controls and caller retirement take ownership immediately. Read status to distinguish accepted start from observed progress; conclusions cite retained source/runtime evidence. Never forces lazy values or evaluates generated expressions.
tools.name: debug_assist

tools.description: Replace source breakpoints for an open buffer, using 1-based lines. Reports pending/verified state; unsaved buffers are marked sourceModified.
tools.name: debug_set_breakpoints

tools.description: Inspect threads, stackTrace, scopes, variables, source or exceptionInfo using generation-scoped handles. Stack and variables require a stopped target. Variable references must come from current scopes/variables responses; lazy handles require explicit evaluation and cannot be expanded here. start/count page results (100 default, 1000 max).
tools.name: debug_inspect

tools.name: lsp_definition

tools.name: lsp_rename

tools.description: List HLS code actions with opaque action IDs; optional endLine/endColumn select a range. A new list expires previous IDs. Only advertised server commands can execute. tools.name: lsp_code_actions

tools.description: Apply a listed action once at its original revision. Checked text edits change buffers only; advertised commands run in HLS and may have server-side effects. Command results report succeeded, commandSucceeded, appliedBatches, partial and changed buffers. Earlier accepted edits remain after failure/cancellation. Resource operations are rejected. Uses live unsaved Haskell source. Input line/column are 1-based Unicode codepoints; raw LSP result coordinates are 0-based UTF-16.
tools.name: lsp_apply_code_action

tools.description: Investigate one Haskell symbol in an open buffer with the same semantic views the human sees: Summary (type), Definitions and References, built from read-only HLS hover/definition/references on live unsaved source. Actions: discover (what is available; optional bufferId,line,column check a position), inspect (bufferId,line,column,revision? -> a page), view (page,view -> another view of that page's object), follow (page,row -> the object or source location that row names; a source location is re-verified against current text), back (page -> the page it came from). Pages are opaque tokens bound to the caller, source revision and a 15 minute lifetime; row numbers are local to one page. Changing, closing or privatizing the buffer expires them. Locations are limited to the workspace.
tools.name: inspect_symbol

tools.name: git_pull

Retains the latest 16 agent jobs; busy includes human Git operations. Only the latest complete review ID can be committed.
tools.name: git_operation_status

tools.description: Operate the editor using up to 64 mouse/key/paste events through its normal input path. Coordinates are 0-based character cells. Keys include characters, Enter, Escape, Tab, ArrowUp/Down/Left/Right, F1..F24, Home/End/PageUp/PageDown/Backspace/Delete/Insert. mods is an array of ctrl/alt/shift. tools.description: Capture the guest-readable editor frame as colorless text and optional PNG. Private cells are redacted in both outputs. tools.name: editor_screen

tools.description: Read provider executable, argument count, environment variable names, connection state, model/config choices and context usage. Secret-labelled values, argument values, environment values and session keys are omitted. Cannot change provider settings.
tools.name: agent_settings

tools.name: docs_list

tools.description: Read a line range from an offline document. Files must be UTF-8 and at most 1 MiB. Responses are capped at 128 Ki characters. Lines start at 1.
tools.name: docs_read

tools.description: Search literal text in offline documentation, with line numbers and enclosing headings. Searches at most 256 files and 16 MiB; partial results are marked. No regex or network access.
tools.name: docs_search

tools.description: Inspect the editor process environment used by newly launched builds, terminals, debuggers and agents. Optional names limits the result; absent names are null. Credential and editor authority values are always redacted. Use before prescribing shell exports or an editor restart.
tools.name: environment_get

tools.description: Set or unset variables for newly launched editor subprocesses. values maps names to strings or null (unset); scope is session (default), project (thc.toml), or global (thc/config.toml). Prefer a project build configuration fix when it makes the dependency discoverable for everyone.

tools.description: Create one inline human question and return questionId/status pending immediately. Continue independent work, then retrieve its status using questionId only. No timeout supplies an answer or approval.

tools.description: Apply strict unified diffs atomically to 1–16 distinct live text buffers at their given revisions, with at most 1048576 patch characters in total. tools.description: List open buffers with paths and unsaved-change state, including untitled buffers.

tools.description: Read live buffer contents including unsaved edits; private conversation fields are redacted and approval buffers are unavailable. Text is paged by 1-based lines (200 default, 1000 maximum), capped at 131072 characters; binary buffers return up to 4096 hex bytes from byteOffset.
tools.name: read_buffer

tools.description: Read an explicitly readable prepared text window by logical window-text lines; private regions are redacted. Defaults to the active window, 200 lines; maximum 1000 lines and 131072 characters. Source windows use read_buffer.
tools.name: read_window

tools.description: Write UTF-8 input to a shared terminal. Input may execute commands or send control characters.
tools.name: terminal_input

tools.description: List shared Ghostty terminals, buffer IDs, and exit codes.
tools.name: terminal_list

tools.description: Read retained terminal output (at most 128 KiB per call) and exit code. Offset and limit count bytes; offset is relative to the retained tail. truncated indicates dropped earlier bytes.

tools.description: Start an executable and argument array in a shared Ghostty terminal; no implicit shell. cwd defaults to the project. Returns terminalId and opens its window.
tools.name: terminal_start

tools.description: Terminate a shared terminal process, retaining its output window.
tools.name: terminal_stop

Pause/stop revoke assistance and request a pause if running; reveal shows its evidence without stepping. Manual debugger controls and caller retirement take ownership immediately. Read status to distinguish accepted start from observed progress; conclusions cite retained source/runtime evidence. Never forces lazy values or evaluates generated expressions.

Omitted follow is unchanged; false keeps asynchronous stops in the background. Any view requires the current generation; source/stack/scopes also require a stopped target. follow=true resumes future automatic following; use view=source to reveal now. Pause/stop revoke assistance and request a pause if running; reveal shows its evidence without stepping. Manual debugger controls and caller retirement take ownership immediately. tools.name: lsp_rename

tools.description: List HLS code actions with opaque action IDs; optional endLine/endColumn select a range. A new list expires previous IDs. Only advertised server commands can execute. Command results report succeeded, commandSucceeded, appliedBatches, partial and changed buffers. Earlier accepted edits remain after failure/cancellation. Resource operations are rejected. Uses live unsaved Haskell source. Input line/column are 1-based Unicode codepoints; raw LSP result coordinates are 0-based UTF-16.
tools.name: lsp_apply_code_action

tools.description: Investigate one Haskell symbol in an open buffer with the same semantic views the human sees: Summary (type), Definitions and References, built from read-only HLS hover/definition/references on live unsaved source. Actions: discover (what is available; optional bufferId,line,column check a position), inspect (bufferId,line,column,revision? -> a page), view (page,view -> another view of that page's object), follow (page,row -> the object or source location that row names; a source location is re-verified against current text), back (page -> the page it came from). Pages are opaque tokens bound to the caller, source revision and a 15 minute lifetime; row numbers are local to one page. Changing, closing or privatizing the buffer expires them. Locations are limited to the workspace.
tools.name: inspect_symbol

tools.name: git_pull

tools.name: git_merge

tools.name: git_review

tools.description: List editor window IDs, titles, buffer IDs, geometry, active window and side panels.
tools.name: list_windows

tools.description: Read up to 131072 selected characters and cursor offsets in an editor window; truncated reports a larger selection. coordinateSpace distinguishes source from rendered-markdown offsets; a pending Markdown view refuses the read. Defaults to the active window.
tools.name: read_selection

tools.description: Read connection, stop state, generation, selected frame, follow mode, capabilities, breakpoints and recent output.
tools.name: debug_status

tools.description: Set automatic source following (initially true), or reveal source/stack/scopes/output from the shared session. Omitted follow is unchanged; false keeps asynchronous stops in the background. Any view requires the current generation; source/stack/scopes also require a stopped target. follow=true resumes future automatic following; use view=source to reveal now. Presentation does not resume, relaunch or advance generation.

tools.description: Launch the configured THC target, or a general DAP adapter JSON configuration. Fails if a session is already active.
tools.name: debug_launch

tools.description: Attach to a loopback DAP adapter (127.0.0.1:4711 by default).

tools.description: Continue, step, pause or disconnect the current debug generation. Accepted does not mean the next stop has occurred; inspect status afterwards.
tools.name: debug_control

tools.description: Run bounded goal-directed inspection and stepping with the selected System One supplier. Start requires an exact paused generation and a goal. Pause/stop revoke assistance and request a pause if running; reveal shows its evidence without stepping. Manual debugger controls and caller retirement take ownership immediately. Read status to distinguish accepted start from observed progress; conclusions cite retained source/runtime evidence. Never forces lazy values or evaluates generated expressions.

tools.description: Replace source breakpoints for an open buffer, using 1-based lines. Reports pending/verified state; unsaved buffers are marked sourceModified.
tools.name: debug_set_breakpoints

tools.description: Inspect threads, stackTrace, scopes, variables, source or exceptionInfo using generation-scoped handles. Stack and variables require a stopped target. tools.name: debug_inspect

tools.name: lsp_hover

tools.description: Find HLS definitions. Uses live unsaved Haskell source. Input line/column are 1-based Unicode codepoints; raw LSP result coordinates are 0-based UTF-16.
tools.name: lsp_definition

tools.name: lsp_type_definition

tools.name: lsp_document_symbols

tools.name: lsp_rename

tools.description: List HLS code actions with opaque action IDs; optional endLine/endColumn select a range. A new list expires previous IDs. Only advertised server commands can execute. tools.name: lsp_code_actions

Command results report succeeded, commandSucceeded, appliedBatches, partial and changed buffers. Earlier accepted edits remain after failure/cancellation. Resource operations are rejected. Uses live unsaved Haskell source. Input line/column are 1-based Unicode codepoints; raw LSP result coordinates are 0-based UTF-16.
tools.name: lsp_apply_code_action

tools.description: Investigate one Haskell symbol in an open buffer with the same semantic views the human sees: Summary (type), Definitions and References, built from read-only HLS hover/definition/references on live unsaved source. Pages are opaque tokens bound to the caller, source revision and a 15 minute lifetime; row numbers are local to one page. Changing, closing or privatizing the buffer expires them. Locations are limited to the workspace.
tools.name: inspect_symbol

tools.name: git_pull

tools.description: Merge one named local or remote-tracking branch after checking incoming changes and clean saved files. No raw revision syntax, URL or options. Conflicts remain for resolution; no automatic abort. Poll actual exit, HEAD and conflict count.

tools.description: Operate the editor using up to 64 mouse/key/paste events through its normal input path. Coordinates are 0-based character cells.
